title: A presentation whose conormal map is split injective gives a smooth algebra
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n\ge0$, $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra and $\alpha:P\to S$ a surjective homomorphism of $R$-algebras whose kernel $I$ is a finitely generated ideal of $P$. Then $I/I^2$ is an $S=P/I$-module, and the map $\mathrm d_\alpha:I/I^2\to S\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}$, $g\bmod I^2\mapsto1\otimes\mathrm dg$ ($\Omega_{P/R}$ and $\mathrm d$ as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], $S\otimes_P-$ the base change along $\alpha$ [def-weil-module-base-change]), is well defined and $S$-linear. If $\mathrm d_\alpha$ has an $S$-linear left inverse, i.e. there is an $S$-linear map $\lambda:S\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}\to I/I^2$ with $\lambda\circ\mathrm d_\alpha=\mathrm{id}_{I/I^2}$, then $S$ is a smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].
